<!-- 👋 Hi, thanks for sending a PR to mocha! 💖.
Please fill out all fields below and make sure each item is true and [x] checked.
Otherwise we may not be able to review your PR. -->

## PR Checklist

- [x] Addresses an existing open issue: fixes #5468
- [x] That issue was marked as [`status: accepting prs`](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22status%3A+accepting+prs%22)
- [x] Steps in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) were taken

## Overview

This PR removes the `log-symbols` dependency, inlining its functionality. This removes `chalk` and its many subdependencies from the dependency tree.

~We no longer check for explicit Unicode support. In case anyone is running Mocha from the Windows legacy command prompt (and possibly PowerShell?), the characters may not show up properly.~ `is-unicode-supported` is used to switch between rich unicode emojis and traditional characters.

I also noticed that the symbols do not respect `Base.useColors`, and never seem to have done so. This might be something to look into in the future.

author: toxicmushroom
body:
This now adds support for custom modes and custom modelines as discussed in #333.
Allowing users to run niri with a mode that their monitor does not advertise.
Users should be **CAUTIOUS** when using this, running monitors out of spec can result in damage. 

Current added config syntaxes:

**Custom mode**
```kdl
output "eDP-1" {
    mode custom=true "1920x1080@60"
}
```

**Modeline**
```kdl
output "eDP-1" {
    modeline 173.00  1920 2048 2248 2576  1080 1083 1088 1120 "-hsync" "+vsync"
}
```

Current added IPC commands:

**Custom mode**
`niri msg output <OUTPUT> custom-mode 1920x1080@60`

**Modeline**
`niri msg output <OUTPUT> modeline 173.00  1920 2048 2248 2576  1080 1083 1088 1120 "-hsync" "+vsync"`



Please let me know anything you'd want me to modify/fix/add/remove :), I tried incorporating the comments Yalter left on the preceding PR #1283 by cmeissl.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a comprehensive test suite covering all functions and procedures in the pure-utils library, addressing the requirement to "розроби тести для всіх функцій" (develop tests for all functions).

## Overview

The test suite provides thorough validation of ~106 functions and 18 procedures across all functional categories in pure-utils, ensuring reliability, performance, and correctness of the codebase.

## Test Coverage

### Functions Tested by Category:
- **String & Text Processing** (12 functions): `stringSplitToLines`, `stringFindCommentsPositions`, `stringSplitMultiLineComment`, etc.
- **Objects & Metadata** (25 functions): `metadataGetObjectName`, `metadataGetObjectType`, `metadataGetColumns`, etc.
- **Modules & Code Analysis** (18 functions): `modulesSplitToLines`, `modulesGetDescriptionFromComments`, `modulesFindSimilar`, etc.
- **Index Functions** (10 functions): `indexesGetConventionNames`, `indexesGetMissing`, `indexesGetSpaceUsed`, etc.
- **Script Generation & Utilities** (12+ functions): `stringGetCreateTempScript`, `tablesGetScript`, `xeGetErrors`, etc.

### Procedures Tested:
All 18 procedures including `help`, `errorHandler`, metadata management procedures (`metadataSetTableDescription`, `metadataSetColumnDescription`, etc.), and module management procedures.

## Test Infrastructure

### Core Framework
- **TestFramework.sql**: Assertion functions (`#AssertEquals`, `#AssertNotNull`, `#AssertTrue`) with clear pass/fail reporting
- **RunAllTests.sql**: Master test runner executing all test suites with comprehensive reporting
- **QuickTest.sql**: Lightweight test runner for rapid development validation

### Test Types Implemented
- **Unit Tests**: Individual function validation with edge cases and error conditions
- **Integration Tests**: Cross-function consistency and workflow validation
- **Performance Tests**: Large dataset handling (1000+ lines), timing validation, memory efficiency
- **Error Handling Tests**: NULL values, non-existent objects, permission limitations

## Example Test Validation

```sql
-- String processing with edge cases
DECLARE @TestString NVARCHAR(MAX) = 'Line 1' + CHAR(13) + CHAR(10) + 'Line 2';
DECLARE @ResultCount INT;
SELECT @ResultCount = COUNT(*) FROM util.stringSplitToLines(@TestString, 1);
EXEC #AssertEquals '2', CAST(@ResultCount AS NVARCHAR(10)), 'stringSplitToLines basic functionality';

-- Metadata consistency validation
DECLARE @HelpType1 NVARCHAR(2) = util.metadataGetObjectType('util.help');
DECLARE @HelpType2 NVARCHAR(2) = (SELECT type FROM sys.objects WHERE object_id = OBJECT_ID('util.help'));
EXEC #AssertEquals @HelpType2, @HelpType1, 'Object type consistency across functions';
```

## Performance & Reliability Features

- **Graceful Error Handling**: Tests handle permission issues and missing configurations appropriately
- **Performance Benchmarks**: Generous time limits with execution time reporting
- **Real-World Scenarios**: Tests use actual system objects (sys.objects, sys.columns) for realistic validation
- **CI/CD Ready**: Designed for automated testing pipelines with clear pass/fail reporting

## File Structure

```
Tests/
├── TestFramework.sql           # Core testing framework
├── RunAllTests.sql            # Master test runner  
├── QuickTest.sql              # Quick validation
├── Functions/                 # Function-specific tests
│   ├── StringProcessingTests.sql
│   ├── MetadataTests.sql
│   ├── ModulesTests.sql
│   ├── IndexTests.sql
│   └── ScriptGenerationTests.sql
├── Procedures/ProceduresTests.sql
├── Integration/IntegrationTests.sql
├── Performance/PerformanceTests.sql
└── TESTING.md                 # Comprehensive documentation
```

## Usage

Execute the complete test suite:
```sql
:r Tests\RunAllTests.sql
```

Quick validation during development:
```sql
:r Tests\QuickTest.sql
```

The test suite provides confidence in library functionality and helps maintain code quality as the project evolves, with comprehensive coverage ensuring all pure-utils functions and procedures are thoroughly validated.

body: # Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Samples Pull Request > [!IMPORTANT] > 1. We strictly follow a issue-first approach, please first open an [issue](https://github.com/awslabs/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-samples/issues) relating to this Pull Request. > 2. Once this Pull Request is ready for review please attach `review ready` label to it. Only PRs with `review ready` will be reviewed. **Issue number**: #418 ### Concise description of the PR ``` The statically stored bearer token in the Secrets Manager by default seems to expire in an hour and sometimes user may need to come back and run the MCP remote client after that 1 hour period. The bearer token in secrets manager will be of no use when it expires and the remote client will always error out in the absence of the refresh token flow. This PR fixes it by introducing refresh auth flow to get a fresh bearer_token when the token in SecretsManager expires. ``` ### User experience > Please share what the user experience looks like before and after this change Before the user will see error as desribed in #418. This PR adds comprehensive time and date configuration capabilities, new media tools and codecs, and idempotent installation functionality to the Windows 11 setup script, addressing the need for proper system time setup, modern media support, and safe script re-execution during initial OS configuration.

## What's Added

**Time Configuration Features:**
- **Automatic NTP Time Synchronization** - Configures Windows Time service with `time.windows.com` as the primary time server
- **Automatic Timezone Detection** - Enables location-based timezone configuration through Windows services
- **Enhanced Time Display Format** - Sets 24-hour format with seconds (HH:mm:ss) for better precision
- **Location Services Integration** - Configures location-based timezone updates when possible

**New Media Tools & Codecs:**
- **HandBrake** - Professional video transcoder and converter for various formats
- **HEIF Image Extensions** - Free support for modern HEIF/HEIC image formats from iOS devices
- **HEVC Video Extensions** - Free advanced H.265/HEVC video codec support

**Idempotent Installation System:**
- **Package Installation Checks** - Verifies if packages are already installed before attempting installation
- **Safe Re-execution** - Script can be run multiple times without errors or unnecessary reinstallation
- **Enhanced User Feedback** - Shows "Checking..." status and "already installed" messages for better UX

**New Function: `Configure-TimeSettings`**
```powershell
function Configure-TimeSettings {
    # Enables automatic time sync, timezone detection, and format configuration
    # Includes error handling and cross-platform simulation support
}
```

## User Experience Improvements

- **Updated Banner** - Now includes "🎨 Graphics Design & Media Tools", "🎬 Media Codecs & Extensions", and "🕒 Time & Date Configuration" to reflect expanded functionality
- **Enhanced Summary** - Installation summary now shows time configuration features, new media tools, and codecs alongside software packages
- **Improved Installation Process** - Changed from "Installing..." to "Checking..." with clear status messages for existing vs. newly installed packages
- **Improved Completion Message** - Added time-related verification steps in post-installation guidance

## Documentation Updates

- **README.md** - Added dedicated time configuration section and new media tools with feature descriptions
- **CHANGELOG.md** - Documented new v1.2.0 release with comprehensive feature list including media tools and idempotent installation
- **TESTING.md** - Updated testing guide to include time configuration validation and re-run safety information
- **Script Synopsis** - Updated PowerShell help documentation to reflect new capabilities

## Technical Implementation

The enhanced script now includes:
- Registry modifications for automatic timezone service
- Windows Time service configuration with reliable NTP servers
- Time format customization through International settings
- Package installation verification using `winget list` before attempting installation
- Graceful error handling for settings requiring manual intervention
- Full simulation mode support for cross-platform testing
- Modern media codec support for HEIF/HEIC and HEVC formats

## Why This Matters

This comprehensive enhancement provides:
- **Time Accuracy**: Essential for development work, certificate validation, and log correlation
- **Modern Media Support**: Native support for iOS photos (HEIC) and modern video formats (HEVC)
- **Professional Video Tools**: HandBrake for video transcoding and conversion needs
- **Safe Operations**: Idempotent installation prevents errors and allows safe script re-execution
- **Complete Setup Experience**: Transforms the script from a simple software installer into a comprehensive Windows 11 setup tool

![Updated Script Output](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1fdd8f8-a982-4c3e-9433-4e8483b20a3b)

This enhancement transforms the script from a simple software installer into a comprehensive Windows 11 setup tool that handles application installation, modern media support, critical system configuration, and provides a safe, repeatable installation experience.

- 관련 컨트롤러/시큐리티 설정 소스 읽고 이상 지점 찾기
- 테스트 기대 JSON과 실제 JSON diff 맞추는 수정
- 한두 개 케이스 먼저 복구 후 부분 재실행

원하시면 "회원가입 성공 테스트부터 잡자"처럼 우선순위를 지정해 주시면 거기서 바로 파고들겠습니다. 어떤 항목부터 진행할까요?
User:  스프링의 기본기능인 withMockUser로 mvc 테스트르해결해야하는거아닌가? 밸리데이션도 로드되니가 그걸도해결하고 
AI: 원인 분석을 위해 시큐리티 설정과 AuthControllerTest 파일 일부를 읽겠습니다. 
AI: AuthControllerTest 파일을 찾아 읽어서 @WithMockUser 사용 여부를 확인하겠습니다. 
AI: TodoControllerTest 와 UserControllerTest 도 인증 방식 확인을 위해 조회하겠습니다. 
AI: UserControllerTest도 인증 패턴 확인을 위해 읽겠습니다. 
AI: @WithMockUser로 해결해야 한다는 질문에 대한 핵심: 지금 실패 원인은 단순히 @WithMockUser 부재가 아니라, (1) SecurityConfig에서 너무 많은 엔드포인트를 permitAll 해둔 상태 + (2) WebMvcTest 환경에서 실제 비즈니스 필터/커스텀 Jwt 컨버터가 비활성/모킹된 상태 + (3) Validation/예외 응답 JSON 구조 기대 불일치 때문입니다. 정리와 개선 전략을 아래에 제시합니다.

## 왜 @WithMockUser 가 기대대로 동작하지 않는가
1. SecurityConfig에서 `/api/todos/**` 전체 
AI:  → 실제로는 인증 테스트가 의미가 없어지거나 테스트 기대(401/403)와 실제 동작이 어긋남 (테스트는 401/403 기대).
2. `@WebMvcTest`는 슬라이스 테스트라 Spring Security 필터 체인 중 일부 커스텀 요소(JWT 디코더, 커스텀 컨버터 로직)가 MockBean 처리되어 토큰 기반 흐름 자체가 우회됨.
3. 컨트롤러 테스트에서 서비스/매퍼/리포지토리 대부분 Mock + DTO 응답/예외 포맷이 실제 글로벌 예외 처리기(`@ControllerAdvice`)에서 사용하는 형태와 다를 수 있음 → JsonPath `$.message` 실패.
4. Validation: Form(UrlEncoded) 파라미터 → DTO 바인딩 or Command 매핑 과정이 Mock Mapper에 의해 단순화. 실제 Bean Validation 에러 구조(`fieldErrors`, `code`, `message` 등)와 테스트의 단일 `$.message` 기대 불일치 가능.

## 추천 전략
### 1) 인증/인가 테스트 레벨 구분
- 슬라이스(WebMvcTest): 컨트롤러 레벨 로직/Request 파싱/Validation 포맷만 검증. 인증은 간단히 `@WithMockUser` 혹은 커스텀 `@WithAppUser`.
- 통합(BaseIntegrationTest 확장): 실제 JWT 발급/Redis/Repository/JPA 포함 end-to-end 플로우 검증.

### 2) `@WithAppUser` 커스텀 어노테이션 도입
표준 `@WithMockUser`는 username, roles 정도만 지원. 프로젝트는 UUID 기반 식별자/추가 Claim이 필요할 수 있으므로 SecurityContextFactory 구현:

```java
// src/test/java/point/ttodoApi/shared/security/WithAppUser.java
@Retention(RUNTIME)
@Target({ METHOD, TYPE })
@WithSecurityContext(factory = WithAppUserSecurityContextFactory.class)
public @interface WithAppUser {
  String id() default "ffffffff-ffff-ffff-ffff-ffffffffffff";
  String email() default "test@example.com";
  String[] roles() default {"USER"};
}
```

```java
// src/test/java/point/ttodoApi/shared/security/WithAppUserSecurityContextFactory.java
public class WithAppUserSecurityContextFactory implements WithSecurityContextFactory<WithAppUser> {
  @Override
  public SecurityContext createSecurityContext(WithAppUser annotation) {
    SecurityContext context = SecurityContextHolder.createEmptyContext();
    List<GrantedAuthority> authorities = Arrays.stream(annotation.roles())
        .map(r -> new SimpleGrantedAuthority("ROLE_" + r))
        .toList();
    UserDetails principal = User.builder()
        .username(annotation.id())
        .password("N/A")
        .authorities(authorities)
        .build();
    UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken auth =
        new UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken(principal, principal.getPassword(), principal.getAuthorities());
    context.setAuthentication(auth);
    return context;
  }
}
```

이후 테스트:
```java
@WithAppUser(roles = {"USER","ADMIN"})
void someTest() { ... }
```

### 3) SecurityConfig 테스트 친화 조정 (선택)
- `/api/todos/**`를 전면 permitAll → 실제 비즈니스 요구와 상충. 최소한 쓰기/변경/삭제는 인증 필요하도록 조정:
  ```
  .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/api/todos/**").permitAll()
  .requestMatchers("/api/todos/**").authenticated()
  ```
  혹은 테스트 슬라이스에서는...

</details>

body:
## Overview

This PR fixes all compilation errors in `IRGalleryFragmentCompose.kt` that were preventing the thermal imaging gallery feature from building successfully, and addresses critical performance issues that would cause UI freezing. The fragment is part of the Compose migration effort for the thermal unified module.

## Issues Fixed

### 1. Missing Coil Image Loading Dependencies
The fragment was importing `coil.compose.AsyncImage` and `coil.request.ImageRequest` but the Coil dependency wasn't configured in the module's build.gradle.kts.

**Solution:** Temporarily replaced AsyncImage components with placeholder Box components containing image icons. Added TODO comments for proper Coil integration when Maven repositories are configured.

```kotlin
// Before: AsyncImage with unresolved imports
AsyncImage(model = ImageRequest.Builder(LocalContext.current)...)

// After: Placeholder with clear migration path
Box(/* Thumbnail placeholder (TODO: Replace with AsyncImage when Coil is available) */)
```

### 2. Missing ViewModel StateFlow Properties
The fragment was trying to observe StateFlow properties that didn't exist in `IRGalleryViewModel`:
- `galleryItems`
- `currentDirType`  
- `isLoading`
- `selectedItems`
- `isSelectionMode`
- `isGridView`

**Solution:** Added all required StateFlow properties to the ViewModel while maintaining backward compatibility with existing LiveData patterns.

### 3. Missing ViewModel Methods
The fragment was calling methods that weren't implemented in the ViewModel:
- `changeDirType()`
- `toggleViewMode()`
- `refreshGallery()`
- `toggleItemSelection()`
- `enterSelectionMode()`
- `exitSelectionMode()`
- `deleteSelectedItems()`
- `shareSelectedItems()`
- `openGalleryItem()`

**Solution:** Implemented all missing methods with proper coroutine handling and state management.

### 4. Invalid DirType Enum Reference
The fragment referenced `DirType.TS004` which doesn't exist in the `GalleryRepository.DirType` enum. The enum only contains `TS004_LOCALE` and `TS004_REMOTE`.

**Solution:** Updated all references to use `DirType.TS004_LOCALE` consistently.

### 5. Property Access and Function Call Issues
- `item.size` property doesn't exist on `GalleryBean`
- `item.date` property doesn't exist (should use `timeMillis`)
- Missing `background` import for Compose modifier

**Solution:** 
- Added file size caching system with background calculation
- Updated date formatting to use `item.timeMillis`
- Added missing `background` import

### 6. Performance Issues (P1 Priority)
**Gallery Refresh Threading:** `refreshGallery()` was running filesystem operations on the main thread, potentially freezing UI for hundreds of milliseconds with large galleries.

**File I/O During Composition:** File size calculations were performed synchronously during UI composition, blocking list rendering.

**Solution:** 
- Changed `refreshGallery()` to use `Dispatchers.IO` consistently with other repository calls
- Implemented file size caching system that pre-calculates sizes on background thread
- Replaced synchronous `getFileSize()` calls with instant cache lookups (`getCachedFileSize()`)
- Eliminated all blocking I/O operations from UI composition path

## Files Modified

- **`IRGalleryViewModel.kt`**: Added StateFlow properties, Compose-compatible methods, and file size caching with background threading
- **`IRGalleryFragmentCompose.kt`**: Fixed all compilation errors and replaced blocking I/O with cached lookups
- **`build.gradle.kts`**: Added commented Coil dependency with TODO for future integration

## Testing

All IRGalleryFragmentCompose-specific compilation errors have been resolved:
- ✅ No more "Unresolved reference 'coil'" errors
- ✅ No more "Unresolved reference 'galleryItems'" errors  
- ✅ No more "Unresolved reference 'TS004'" errors
- ✅ No more function invocation and property access errors
- ✅ Performance issues resolved - no main thread blocking during gallery operations

## Migration Path

This PR provides a clean foundation for completing the thermal gallery Compose migration:

1. **Immediate**: All compilation errors resolved, fragment ready for use with optimal performance
2. **Short-term**: Add proper Coil dependency when Maven repositories are configured
3. **Long-term**: Enhance image loading, sharing, and gallery item opening functionality

The changes follow minimal-modification principles while maintaining clean MVVM architecture, ensuring smooth UI performance, and providing clear TODO markers for future enhancements.

## Summary

This PR fixes an issue where users couldn't exit CLI setup prompts using Control-C (Ctrl+C). When accidentally selecting option 2 (Anthropic API key) during initial setup, users had to kill the process externally instead of being able to use the standard Ctrl+C exit.

## Root Cause

The issue was caused by conflicting SIGINT handlers:
1. The main process has a SIGINT handler for non-TUI flows that calls `gracefulExit(130)`
2. The readline interface in `question()` sets up its own SIGINT handler
3. During onboarding prompts, both handlers were active, causing interference

## Solution

Modified the `question()` function in `extensions/cli/src/util/prompt.ts` to:
- Temporarily remove existing SIGINT listeners when starting a prompt
- Set up the readline SIGINT handler for immediate Ctrl+C exit
- Restore original SIGINT listeners after the prompt completes or is interrupted
- Added proper error handling and cleanup

## Changes

- **Fixed**: `question()` function now properly handles SIGINT conflicts
- **Improved**: `questionWithChoices()` now has better error handling for interruptions
- **Enhanced**: Added tests to verify SIGINT behavior and listener restoration
- **Tested**: Verified that original SIGINT listeners are properly restored

## Testing

- Added test case to verify SIGINT handler restoration
- Updated existing skipped test for SIGINT handling
- Manual testing confirms Ctrl+C now works during CLI setup prompts

## Impact

Users can now properly exit CLI setup prompts with Ctrl+C without having to kill the process externally. This improves the overall user experience during the onboarding flow.

Fixes issue reported in Slack: https://continuedev.slack.com/archives/C07A4MCH5JT/p1759192731723179

# Drift Labs Trial – Test Automation Solution

This PR contains a solution for the **Drift Labs trial** using **Playwright** as the test automation framework and **Synpress** to handle wallet interactions.

---

## Pre-requisites

1. **Install dependencies**:

```bash
npm install
```

2. **Run the Drift UI app locally**:

You can refer to the official repository for setup:
https://github.com/drift-labs/drift-ui-template

3. **Phantom Wallet**:

Install Phantom wallet from their offical site:
https://phantom.com

## Setup Wallet Caches

1. In your .env.local file, add the following environment variables with the **seed phrases of pre-funded Solana wallets**:

```
SEED_PHRASE_0="festival weapon obtain citizen bullet demise across science stumble swap toy either"
SEED_PHRASE_1="safe note ignore claim capital loud imitate adapt explain egg curious cart"
SEED_PHRASE_2="since eager wife swim quarter enough coach gift bean host inquiry index"
SEED_PHRASE_3="reunion supply voice buzz faculty coyote session action require verify upon ticket"
SEED_PHRASE_4="congress chat faculty tissue parent exit tobacco strategy ketchup indicate rival glide"
SEED_PHRASE_5="own neither myth grunt suspect fantasy burger base vote sponsor minimum meadow"
SYNPRESS_WALLET_PASSWORD=Tester@1234
```


2. Make the wallet cache generation script executable:

`chmod +x tests/utils/generate_wallet_caches.sh`


3. Run the script to generate wallet caches:

`./tests/utils/generate_wallet_caches.sh`


- This will create wallet caches under the `.cache-synpress` folder.

- Copy the generated **cache IDs** into the `run-tests.sh` file.

- Example usage in `run-tests.sh`:

`run_test "{this_is_the_cache_id}" "create-account-deposit.spec.ts" "TC-CA-001"`

## Running Tests

All tests can be executed with:

`npm run test:drift`


The script will:

1. Execute all tests sequentially.
2. Use the specified SYNPRESS_CACHE_IDs for wallet interactions.
3. Generate JSON reports under /reports for each test.
4. Open a merged HTML report at the end.

Project Structure
```
DRIFT-UI-TEMPLATE/
│
├── .idea/                              # IDE settings (ignored)
├── .cache-synpress/                    # Wallet cache folder
├── next.config.ts                      # Next.js config
├── node_modules/                       # Dependencies
├── playwright-report/                  # Playwright report (default)
├── reports/                            # Custom reports folder
├── tests/
│   ├── base/
│   │   ├── BasePage.ts
│   │   └── BaseTest.ts
│   ├── config/
│   │   └── constants.ts
│   ├── e2e/
│   │   ├── create-account-deposit.spec.ts
│   │   └── place-limit-order.spec.ts
│   ├── helpers/
│   │   └── basic.setup.ts
│   ├── pages/
│   │   ├── HomePage.ts
│   │   ├── PerpetualsPage.ts
│   │   └── UserPage.ts
│   └── utils/
│       ├── generate_wallet_caches.sh
│       └── run-tests.sh
├── package.json
├── package-lock.json
├── playwright.config.ts
└── README.md
```

Notes

Each test in run-tests.sh uses a specific Synpress cache ID to ensure wallet state is preserved.

Make sure the Drift app is running locally before executing the tests.

body:
Closes #627

This PR introduces support for enabling and disabling RocksDB compression, as well as validating these settings on program startup. The issue identified a need for configurable compression and a mechanism to prevent reading databases with mismatched compression schemes.

Previously, RocksDB compression was not explicitly configurable, and any manual change could lead to an unreadable database. This implementation addresses these concerns by providing a clear configuration option, managing compression metadata, and preventing database access if the current configuration's compression setting does not match the stored database metadata.

### Key Changes:

-   **Configuration Option:** Added a `compression: bool` field to `ConfigVisible` in `src/settings.rs` (default `true`), allowing users to easily enable or disable RocksDB compression.
-   **Database Options Update:** Modified `DbOptions` and the `rocksdb_options()` function in `src/storage.rs` to apply the configured compression setting to RocksDB.
-   **Compression Metadata Management:** Implemented `store_compression_metadata()`, `read_compression_metadata()`, and `validate_compression_metadata()` in `src/storage.rs`. These functions manage a `COMPRESSION` metadata file within the database directory to persistently store the compression setting used for that database.
-   **Startup Validation:** Added a validation step in `src/main.rs` that checks for compression scheme mismatches before database migration. If a mismatch is detected, Giganto reports a clear error message and exits, preventing potential data corruption or access to unreadable data.
-   **Function Signature Updates:** Adjusted relevant function signatures (e.g., `db_path_and_option`, `repair_db`) in `src/storage.rs` and updated corresponding test cases in `src/storage/migration.rs` to accommodate the new compression parameter.
-   **Documentation:** Updated `CHANGELOG.md` to describe the new compression configuration option and explicitly note that changing the compression setting for an existing database is not supported and would require recreating the database.

This ensures that Giganto always starts with compatible database settings, enhancing stability and preventing data loss or read issues due to configuration changes.

author: kshitijkapoor8
body:
# Overview

Closes #1

This PR introduces the initial design for inter-task communication between the CAN producer and multiple consumers (e.g., XBee TX, SD logging) using a fixed buffer pool with reference counting. Data is produced once, then fanned out to all interested consumers without copies, and safely returned to the pool when no longer in use. UART setup for the XBee radio is also included, but is less interesting.

# Summary of Changes

- Implemented buffer pool with block messages
- Implemented message queues for cross-task communication
- Added refcnt management and automatic frees for blocks
- Added test random CAN data generation and writes to the buffer pool
- Configured UART
- Added UART writes in xbee_tx task

# Todos

- Read real CAN data
- CAN currently drops packets if queues are full, will look into if this would ever actually happen (it should not, however)

# Notes

- This code has been tested to work with UART (in a jank way, so more testing is nice).
- Design consideration: batching writes for the peripherals is nice, and would currently require those tasks to do some copies to ensure that communication queues do not get full.

## What is the current behavior?

- When the `onToolStart` hook throws errors, the process continues without specific behavior for terminating the flow. 
- Errors like `ToolDeniedError` or other error types within `onToolStart` have limited or inconsistent flow impact. 

## What is the new behavior?

- The process flow now terminates when the `onToolStart` hook throws a `ToolDeniedError`. 
- This change ensures that tool-denial errors effectively stop execution and provide clear feedback in the flow.

fixes #255 

## Notes for reviewers

The following code will cause 403 request preserving the payload by server-hono
```ts    
onToolStart: async ({ tool, args, context }) => {

        throw new ToolDeniedError({
          toolName: tool.name,
          message: "Pro plan required for this tool.",
          code: "TOOL_FORBIDDEN",
          httpStatus: 403,
        });
      }
    },

```

body:
This PR implements a comprehensive FHIR IG-based validation test suite for FML (FHIR Mapping Language) execution as requested in issue #XXX. The test suite provides a complete framework for validating FML execution capabilities using real-world test cases sourced from community FML projects with proper license compliance.

## 🎯 Key Features

### FHIR IG Test Structure
- **FSH TestPlan**: Complete `FMLExecutionValidationTestPlan.fsh` defining test cases, validation requirements, and test data references
- **Test Data Organization**: Structured `input/testdata/` directory with subfolders for different test sources

### Test Case Import and Attribution
- **Automated Import**: `scripts/import-test-data.js` imports test cases from ahdis/matchbox and FHIR/fhir-test-cases repositories
- **License Compliance**: Proper attribution headers for Apache 2.0 (matchbox) and HL7 copyright/CC0 (fhir-test-cases) licenses
- **Repository Explorer**: `scripts/explore-test-repos.js` discovers available test files in external repositories

### Test Data Management
- **File Mapping**: `test-manifest.json` explicitly maps `.map` files to their corresponding input/output test cases
- **Validation Pipeline**: `scripts/validate-test-data.js` ensures test data integrity and validates JSON structure
- **Working Examples**: Two complete test cases (patient and observation transforms) with valid FHIR resources

## 📂 Directory Structure

```
input/
├── fsh/tests/FMLExecutionValidationTestPlan.fsh  # FSH TestPlan definition
├── testdata/                                     # Test data with license attribution
│   ├── examples/                                 # Local MIT-licensed examples
│   │   ├── patient-transform.map                 # FML mapping files
│   │   ├── patient-input.json                    # Input FHIR resources
│   │   └── patient-output.json                   # Expected output resources
│   ├── fhir-test-cases/                         # HL7 licensed test cases
│   ├── matchbox/                                 # Apache 2.0 licensed test cases
│   └── test-manifest.json                        # File mapping configuration
└── README.md                                     # Comprehensive documentation
```

## 🛠 Usage

The test suite includes convenient NPM scripts:

```bash
# Import test cases with proper attribution
npm run import:test-data

# Explore external repositories for available test files
npm run explore:test-repos

# Validate test data integrity and mappings
npm run validate:test-data
```

## 📋 Test Case Structure

Each test case follows standardized naming conventions:
- `*-transform.map` or `*.map` — FML mapping specification
- `*-input.json` — FHIR resource to be mapped
- `*-output.json` — Expected output after applying the map

Files are paired by base name (e.g., `patient-transform.map`, `patient-input.json`, `patient-output.json`) and explicitly mapped in the test manifest.

## 📚 Documentation

- **Published TestPlan**: When published, documentation will be available at `https://litlfred.github.io/fmlrunner/TestPlan/FMLExecutionValidationTestPlan.html`
- **Comprehensive README**: Updated main README with test suite usage and references
- **License Attribution**: All imported files include proper source and license attribution

## ✅ Validation Results

All test cases validate successfully:
- JSON structure validation for input/output files
- FML syntax validation for mapping files
- License attribution verification
- File mapping integrity checks

This implementation provides a solid foundation for comprehensive FML execution testing while maintaining full compliance with external project licensing requirements.

**Note**: This implementation uses FHIR TestPlan resources only, without TestScript resources, as requested.

author: tigrannajaryan
body:
Resolves https://github.com/splunk/stef/issues/198

This adds "delta" as a type modifier for int64/uint64 type. Specified once it will make the codec use delta encoding (i.e. on-the-wire values are the deltas from previous values). Specified twice it will make the code use delta-of-delta encoding. If unspecified the value is recorded as is. The "delta delta" specifier matches the current behavior (before the change).

We essentially end up with 3 different codes for int64/uint64 types, see Int64Encoder/Int64DeltaEncoder/Int64DeltaDeltaEncoder family.

This allows schema designer to choose the right codec for each particular field. Timestamps for example are best encoded as "delta delta" since they tend to monotonically increase and "delta of delta" collapses to values close to zero. "delta" is more suitable for varying values that are not monotonic tend to change slowly (e.g. Duration, which naturally is already a delta of timestamp). Small-values enums are best encoded without any modifier, applying delta is unnecessary overhead.

So, all 3 codecs have their own uses.

The improvement of Profile schema after applying the right codec to each field:
```

author: bdash
body:
A new activity is added that will remove calls to `objc_retain`, `objc_release`, `objc_autorelease`, and related functions. It is disabled by default due to the fact it changes the semantics of the code. It can be enabled on a per-function basis via the Function Settings context menu or command palette entry, or it can be enabled in Open with Options or in user settings if a user would prefer it be on for an entire file or for all files they open.

For now the activity is only eligible within arm64 binaries. Supporting x86_64 will require matching some slightly different IL patterns.

author: iasthc
body:
This pull request introduces support for adding custom labels and annotations to Helm release manifests during installation. The main changes include updating the Helm release installation logic to accept and apply these metadata values, defining new constants for standardized label and annotation keys, and ensuring the new functionality is covered in tests.

**Helm release installation enhancements:**

* The `Install` method in both the `ReleaseRepo` interface (`internal/core/application_release.go`) and its implementation (`internal/data/kube/helm_release.go`) now accepts `labels` and `annotations` as additional parameters, allowing custom metadata to be injected into release manifests. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-219906e466347b1e86889aba5646bedd7728884aea65b1ffd5f3e9d98faa6641L22-R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2f33fdda4f8dcb580161a379c509fbd771d53dd3d785d3c80d9cb6cf667ed705L64-R108)
* A new `postRenderer` type is introduced to apply the provided labels and annotations to all manifest nodes after rendering, using `kustomize/kyaml` for YAML manipulation.

**Standardization of metadata keys:**

* New constants for label and annotation keys are defined in `internal/core/const.go`, including `ApplicationReleaseLLMDModelNameLabel` and `ApplicationReleaseChartRefAnnotation`, to ensure consistent usage across the codebase.

**Release creation logic updates:**

* The `CreateRelease` method now constructs and passes the appropriate labels and annotations based on the release context, such as including the model name for specific chart references.

**Dependency management:**

* The `go.mod` file is updated to add a direct dependency on `sigs.k8s.io/kustomize/kyaml`, which is required for post-rendering manifest manipulation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-33ef32bf6c23acb95f5902d7097b7a1d5128ca061167ec0716715b0b9eeaa5f6R51) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-33ef32bf6c23acb95f5902d7097b7a1d5128ca061167ec0716715b0b9eeaa5f6L246)

**Test coverage:**

* Unit tests for Helm release installation are updated to use the new method signature, ensuring the changes are properly tested. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5f2c7b380a882aced4efed20b96a8594c57180e6ad0ecd6374c23f40452a0c27L72-R72) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5f2c7b380a882aced4efed20b96a8594c57180e6ad0ecd6374c23f40452a0c27L90-R90) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5f2c7b380a882aced4efed20b96a8594c57180e6ad0ecd6374c23f40452a0c27L163-R163)

author: petrex
body:
This pull request introduces improvements to shell configuration files for both Zsh and Fish, focusing on safer plugin loading, enhanced fuzzy finder (fzf) integration, and more robust syntax highlighting. It also adds user information to Git configuration. The main themes are plugin and tool integration, conditional loading for better reliability, and configuration enhancements.

**Plugin and Tool Integration:**

* Added fzf integration to both `zsh/.zshrc` and `fish/.config/fish/config.fish`, including conditional sourcing of key bindings and completion scripts for improved command-line navigation and search. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-aa540a91ec15311e6a566dd406c5999db0b6db04ad157b39e7f6babe2d727740R55-R66) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a97a9ea9888a87dacad227d522c51ca9a1b3b4be74499a68a228d64a3efdb47eR26-R33)

**Safer and Conditional Loading:**

* Updated `zsh/.config/zsh/plugins.zsh` to only load plugins if the `plug` function is available, preventing errors if Zap is not loaded.
* Modified `zsh/.zshrc` to source `.zshrc.local` only if the file exists, avoiding potential errors.

**Configuration Enhancements:**

* Improved syntax highlighting in `zsh/.config/zsh/colors.zsh` by conditionally setting regexp highlighting based on the presence of abbreviation variables, making highlighting more robust.
* Added user name and email to `git/.gitconfig` for proper Git author information.

## Summary
This PR fixes critical syntax errors and scope issues in the `AIQuestionGenerator` class that were preventing successful compilation while preserving all existing functionality.

- Added missing `parseCandidate` method implementation
- Added consistent error handling with proper try-catch structure

- **Updated** LLM service references from inconsistent `dsIntService` to standardized `deepseek`
- **Updated** error handling flow to use proper continue statements in catch blocks
- **Updated** method calls from non-existent `generateQuestion` to correct `complete` method

- **Refactored** try-catch blocks to proper JavaScript syntax
- **Refactored** parsing logic to be contained within appropriate scopes

async generateOptions(questionText: string): Promise<GeneratedOptions> {

    } catch (err) { // Proper catch
      continue;
    }
  }
}
```

- Multiple parsing strategies (lines, separators, fallback)
- Same fallback options structure
- Silent error handling
- Normalization and text processing

- Updated all relevant repositories and view models to read from the new CSV data sources.
- Removed the now-obsolete `AllegationProvider`.
- Updated documentation to reflect the new data architecture.
- Fixed a persistent test failure by moving an instrumented test to the correct source set.
- Fixed a type mismatch error in the `CaseViewModel` that was causing build failures.

This pull request primarily refactors logging throughout the `internal/services/utils.go` file, replacing direct `fmt.Printf` and `fmt.Println` calls with the structured `gl.Log` function. It also comments out or removes several sections related to volume management and environment variable configuration for database services, particularly for RabbitMQ and Redis. These changes aim to standardize logging and simplify service setup logic.

**Logging improvements:**

* Replaced all `fmt.Printf` and `fmt.Println` statements with `gl.Log` for consistent logging across service utility functions, including port availability, service status checks, file creation, and Docker activation timeout messages. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5f84ba307bf664282003a6a8d6dbb427b477a3c01e5ab1a8fc71969e6f81d14dL80-R83) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5f84ba307bf664282003a6a8d6dbb427b477a3c01e5ab1a8fc71969e6f81d14dL92-R92) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5f84ba307bf664282003a6a8d6dbb427b477a3c01e5ab1a8fc71969e6f81d14dL128-R128) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-5f84ba307bf664282003a6a8d6dbb427b477a3c01e5ab1a8fc71969e6f81d14dL329-R254) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-5f84ba307bf664282003a6a8d6dbb427b477a3c01e5ab1a8fc71969e6f81d14dL592-R517)

**Service and volume management simplification:**

* Commented out or removed logic for setting up RabbitMQ and Redis volumes, including environment variable assignments and volume bindings when starting containers. This affects how volumes are handled for these services during setup. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5f84ba307bf664282003a6a8d6dbb427b477a3c01e5ab1a8fc71969e6f81d14dL351-R278) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5f84ba307bf664282003a6a8d6dbb427b477a3c01e5ab1a8fc71969e6f81d14dL419-R364) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5f84ba307bf664282003a6a8d6dbb427b477a3c01e5ab1a8fc71969e6f81d14dL504-R429)
* Removed or commented out legacy code for PostgreSQL volume and initialization script setup, streamlining the database service configuration process.

**Other changes:**

* Modified the volume filtering logic in `GetVolumesList` to only include the `gdbase-pg-data` volume, commenting out the check for `gdbase-redis-data`.
* Added a package documentation comment to `internal/models/dsts.go` for improved codebase clarity.

body:
# Add unnecessary_allof_ref_wrapper lint rule for modern JSON Schema

## Summary

Implements a new lint rule that detects and removes unnecessary `allOf` wrappers around `$ref` keywords in JSON Schema versions 2019-09 and later. 

Historically, up to Draft 7, the `$ref` keyword overrode sibling keywords, forcing developers to wrap `$ref` in applicators like `allOf`. This is no longer necessary in modern JSON Schema versions where `$ref` can have siblings.

**Example transformation:**
```json
// Before
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "allOf": [{ "$ref": "https://example.com" }]
}

// After  
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$ref": "https://example.com"
}
```

The rule only applies when:
- Schema uses 2019-09 or 2020-12 vocabularies
- `allOf` contains exactly one branch with only `$ref` (no other properties)
- No sibling `$ref` exists at the same level as `allOf`

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify schema version detection** - Test that the rule correctly identifies 2019-09/2020-12 schemas and ignores Draft 7
- [ ] **Test JSON transformation logic** - Verify the rule correctly extracts `$ref` and handles `allOf` cleanup in various scenarios
- [ ] **Check edge cases** - Test with malformed schemas, empty `allOf` arrays, and complex nested structures
- [ ] **Regression testing** - Ensure existing lint rules and schema processing continue to work correctly

### Notes

**Link to Devin run:** https://staging.itsdev.in/sessions/774ab070b19643a090949283895d50ed

**Requested by:** @jviotti

The implementation follows existing lint rule patterns and includes comprehensive test coverage for both positive cases (where transformation should occur) and negative cases (where it should not). All tests pass and the code has been formatted according to project standards.

author: ubinix-warun
body:
This pull request introduces significant improvements to the `grid_bot.py` trading bot, focusing on better handling of high-priced asset purchases and systematic management of leftover "dust" assets. It also includes parameter tuning for trading thresholds and polling intervals, as well as a new user guide for setting system time. The most important changes are grouped below:

**1. High-priced asset handling and dust management:**

* Added a "high-priced buy rule": for assets where `best_ask` ≥ `HIGH_PRICE_THRESHOLD` (default 1000 USDT), the bot now uses `MARKET BUY` with `quoteOrderQty` to avoid insufficient funds errors, and calculates average price from cost/filled. (`grid_bot.py`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7bf53794e3e68a155a602cba0d1bdc581a349d27cf4c188acb86a9be1ea0b1eaL11-R54) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7bf53794e3e68a155a602cba0d1bdc581a349d27cf4c188acb86a9be1ea0b1eaR737-R779)
* Introduced dust ledger functionality: the bot now logs any leftover asset quantities ("dust") that cannot be sold due to rounding, minimum quantity, or notional constraints into `dust_ledger.csv`, including details like timestamp, symbol, remainder quantity, cost, and reason. (`grid_bot.py`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7bf53794e3e68a155a602cba0d1bdc581a349d27cf4c188acb86a9be1ea0b1eaL11-R54) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7bf53794e3e68a155a602cba0d1bdc581a349d27cf4c188acb86a9be1ea0b1eaR581-R637) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7bf53794e3e68a155a602cba0d1bdc581a349d27cf4c188acb86a9be1ea0b1eaR880-R900) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-7bf53794e3e68a155a602cba0d1bdc581a349d27cf4c188acb86a9be1ea0b1eaR910-R934) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-7bf53794e3e68a155a602cba0d1bdc581a349d27cf4c188acb86a9be1ea0b1eaR945-R971)

**2. Trading logic and parameter tuning:**

* Increased `MAX_OPEN_ORDERS` from 10 to 20, and lowered the z-score threshold for CVD from 2 to 1.5, making the bot more sensitive and able to open more simultaneous deals. (`grid_bot.py`, [grid_bot.pyL74-R93](diffhunk://#diff-7bf53794e3e68a155a602cba0d1bdc581a349d27cf4c188acb86a9be1ea0b1eaL74-R93))
* Increased `TRADES_POLL_MS` from 1200ms to 2000ms, reducing the frequency of recent trades polling for efficiency. (`grid_bot.py`, [grid_bot.pyL93-R109](diffhunk://#diff-7bf53794e3e68a155a602cba0d1bdc581a349d27cf4c188acb86a9be1ea0b1eaL93-R109))

**3. User experience and documentation:**

* Added a new user guide file `วิธีตั้งเวลาเครื่อง.txt`, with instructions for setting system time on macOS and Windows to ensure bot accuracy.

These enhancements improve the bot's reliability when trading high-priced assets, provide transparency for unsold asset fragments, and offer better usability for end users.

author: balaraj74
body:
### What's the problem?

I ran into an issue where cloud-init instructions were being silently ignored when launching VMs. The VM would start up instantly instead of taking time to install packages, and there were no errors to indicate what went wrong.

After some debugging, I tracked it down to a race condition: QEMU was starting before the cloud-init ISO file was fully synced to disk. The ISO gets created in `BaseVirtualMachineFactory::configure()`, but by the time `QemuVirtualMachine::start()` runs, the filesystem hasn't always flushed the write yet.

### How I fixed it

The fix is pretty straightforward:

1. **Verify after creation** - Right after creating the ISO, we try to open and read it. If that fails, we throw an error immediately with a clear message. This catches the problem early instead of silently continuing.

2. **Retry on startup** - When the VM is starting, if the ISO file isn't found on the first check, we wait 100ms and try again. This gives the filesystem time to sync. If it's still missing after that, then we throw an error.

3. **Added a test** - I added a regression test (`cloudInitIsoIsImmediatelyAccessible`) that verifies the ISO can be read immediately after calling `configure()`. This should catch any similar issues in the future.

### Changes made

- `src/platform/backends/shared/base_virtual_machine_factory.cpp` - Added validation after ISO creation
- `src/platform/backends/qemu/qemu_virtual_machine.cpp` - Added retry logic with 100ms delay  
- `tests/test_base_virtual_machine_factory.cpp` - Added regression test

All existing tests still pass, and the new test validates the fix.

Fixes #4396

The actor model forces unnecessary serialization of rw access to rocksdb. Rocks handles concurrent access and this serialization was resulting in code complexity and was exposing us to high tail latencies.

By directly accessing database through an Arc hanlde simplifies code and avoids enqueueing of requests behind a single slow one.

author: necrophillip
body:
Esta es una refactorización completa de la pestaña de Sintonización de PID, incorporando una lógica de análisis de respuesta al escalón superior proporcionada por el usuario y asegurando que los tres escenarios de datos de entrada se manejen correctamente.

Cambios Clave:

1.  **Lógica de Análisis de Respuesta al Escalón Mejorada:**
    -   Se ha reemplazado la función `extract_step_response_from_log` por una implementación mucho más robusta basada en el código del usuario.
    -   El nuevo método detecta múltiples deflexiones de stick, realiza un ajuste de primer orden para estimar `tau`, reajusta la ventana de análisis, y luego promedia las respuestas para obtener una curva representativa.
    -   Se ajustan modelos de primer y segundo orden a la respuesta promedio, y los parámetros resultantes (K, τ, ωn, ζ) se muestran en la interfaz de usuario.

2.  **Flujo de Trabajo de Tres Vías Corregido y Funcional:**
    -   **CLI + Blackbox:** Si ambos archivos están presentes, la herramienta utiliza los PIDs del CLI como base y los refina comparando la respuesta simulada con la respuesta real del Blackbox.
    -   **Solo CLI:** Si solo se carga un volcado de CLI, la herramienta simula la respuesta y propone un ajuste.
    -   **Solo Blackbox:** Si solo se carga un registro de Blackbox, la herramienta utiliza el nuevo análisis de respuesta al escalón para proponer PIDs basados en las métricas y el perfil del dron.

3.  **Corrección de Errores Críticos:**
    -   Se ha solucionado el error de carga de archivos (`AttributeError` / `NameError`) que impedía cargar registros de Blackbox directamente desde la pestaña.
    -   Se ha restaurado la lógica de `parse_dump` para que maneje correctamente los perfiles de Betaflight, asegurando una lectura precisa de los PIDs.

4.  **Interfaz de Usuario Mejorada:**
    -   La interfaz de usuario ahora muestra las curvas de respuesta ajustadas de 1er y 2do orden.
    -   Se ha añadido una nueva sección para mostrar los parámetros del modelo de función de transferencia (K, τ, ωn, ζ).
    -   El flujo de trabajo sigue siendo automático y se han mantenido las mejoras estéticas (botones redimensionados) y funcionales (menú desplegable para registros precargados).

## Summary

This PR implements two critical reliability improvements for the quiz system:

**Task 2: Session Validation Enhancement (Issue #35)**
- Improved session validation between quiz and recommendations
- Added comprehensive session state validation
- Implemented legacy session format transformation
- Enhanced error handling with detailed logging

**Task 3: OpenAI Reranking Reliability (Issue #33)**  
- Added input sanitization for fragrance descriptions
- Implemented explicit exponential backoff retry logic (1s, 2s, 4s delays)
- Enhanced error logging with parse position tracking
- Added success rate monitoring with 95% target
- All structured output improvements in place

## Changes Made

### Session Validation (Task 2)
- Enhanced `lib/session-validation.ts` with comprehensive state checks
- Added legacy session format transformation for backward compatibility
- Improved quiz action validation in `app/actions/quiz.ts`
- Added recommendation validation in `app/actions/recommendations.ts`
- Comprehensive test coverage in `tests/session-validation.test.ts`

### OpenAI Reranking (Task 3)
- Added `RerankResult` interface with score and explanation fields
- Implemented `sanitizeDescription()` to remove control characters and escape JSON special characters
- Updated retry logic to 3 explicit attempts with 1s, 2s, 4s delays
- Enhanced JSON parse error logging with position and response preview
- Added hourly success rate monitoring with metrics reset
- Comprehensive test coverage in `tests/openai-reranking.test.ts`

## Testing

### Task 2: Session Validation
- All 9 session validation tests passing ✓
- Handles legacy formats correctly ✓
- Proper error messages for invalid states ✓

### Task 3: OpenAI Reranking  
- All 10 OpenAI reranking tests passing ✓
- Input sanitization verified ✓
- Retry logic with exponential backoff confirmed ✓
- Error logging enhanced ✓
- Success rate monitoring active ✓

## Related

- Spec: `.agent-os/specs/2025-09-30-quiz-performance-fixes/`

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

## Summary

Enhanced the `gscloud info` command to display additional resource metrics beyond just object counts, providing users with more detailed information about their infrastructure at a glance.

## Changes

The `info` command now displays:
- **Servers**: Total count, CPU cores, and memory (in GiB)
- **Storages**: Total count and capacity (in GiB)
- **IP addresses**: Total count
- **Platform services**: Total count

### Before
```
OBJECT             COUNT
Platform services  0
Servers            18
Storages           24
IP addresses       2
```

### After
```
OBJECT             COUNT  CORES  MEMORY (GiB)  CAPACITY (GiB)
Platform services  0      -      -             -
Servers            18     36     72            -
Storages           24     -      -             240
IP addresses       2      -      -             -
```

## Implementation Details

The data (cores, memory, capacity) was already being collected by the backend API calls but wasn't being displayed in the table output. This change:

1. Adds three new columns to the output table: `CORES`, `MEMORY (GiB)`, and `CAPACITY (GiB)`
2. Displays the relevant metrics for each resource type, showing "-" for non-applicable fields
3. Updates the help text example to reflect the new output format
4. Maintains backward compatibility - JSON output automatically includes all collected fields

The implementation is minimal and surgical, modifying only the table rendering logic without changing any data collection or JSON output behavior.

## Resolves

Fixes issue requesting that `gscloud info` show more details about resources, specifically:
- ✅ Project name and API location (already displayed)
- ✅ Number of cores for servers
- ✅ Memory for servers in GiB
- ✅ Storage capacity in GiB

## Overview

This PR implements the complete **Phase 1: Infrastructure & Configuration** of GIM_AI, a comprehensive AI-powered gym management system. Following the sequential implementation plan outlined in the issue, I've completed Prompts 1-4, establishing a production-ready foundation for the system.

## What's Been Implemented

### 🗂️ PROMPT 1: Project Structure & Initial Configuration

Created a complete project foundation with:
- **32 organized directories** covering all system components (database, n8n-workflows, whatsapp, frontend, scripts, docs, tests)
- **Full package.json** with 40+ dependencies including Supabase, Express, WhatsApp SDK, Bull queues, Winston logging
- **Docker Compose** setup with PostgreSQL, Redis, n8n, and API services for local development
- **Environment configuration** with 80+ documented variables in `.env.example`
- **Development tools**: ESLint, Prettier, Jest configuration
- **Main Express server** with health checks and webhook endpoints
- **Comprehensive README** with stack documentation and quick start guide

### 🗄️ PROMPT 2: Complete Database Schema

Built an optimized PostgreSQL database with:
- **11 production tables**: members, instructors, classes, reservations, checkins, payments, feedback, incidents, instructor_skills, replacements_log, whatsapp_messages
- **60+ optimized indexes** including B-tree, GIN (for arrays/JSON), partial, and composite indexes
- **11 SQL functions** for business logic:
  - `calculate_morosidad()` - Calculate delinquency percentage
  - `calculate_ocupacion_franja()` - Calculate occupancy by time slot
  - `calculate_nps()` - Net Promoter Score calculation
  - `get_member_debt_status()` - Individual debt status
  - `detect_valley_hours()` - Identify low-occupancy time slots
  - `suggest_replacement_instructors()` - AI-powered instructor matching
  - And 5 more utility functions
- **Row Level Security (RLS)** policies for data protection
- **Automatic triggers** for updated_at timestamps
- **Sample data** with 10 members, 5 instructors, and multiple classes for testing
- **Migration scripts** ready for Supabase deployment

### 📱 PROMPT 3: WhatsApp Business API Client

Developed a complete WhatsApp integration with:
- **5 core modules**:
  - `sender.js` - Message sending with queue and exponential backoff retry
  - `webhook.js` - Incoming message processing with Meta signature verification
  - `logger.js` - Comprehensive logging to Supabase with delivery tracking
  - `templates.js` - 13 pre-defined HSM templates management
  - `rate-limiter.js` - Intelligent rate limiting (max 2 messages/day, 9-21h window)
- **13 WhatsApp templates** for all gym operations:
  - Welcome messages, check-in confirmations
  - Class reminders (24h advance)
  - Payment reminders (D0/D3/D7 collection sequences)
  - Contextual post-workout collection
  - Waitlist notifications, satisfaction surveys
  - Reactivation campaigns, instructor changes
- **Business rules enforcement**: automatic business hours compliance, opt-in/opt-out handling
- **Bull queue integration** with Redis for reliable message delivery

### 🤖 PROMPT 4: n8n Workflow Configuration

Implemented 3 production-ready automation workflows:

**Check-in Flow** (`checkin-flow.json`):
- Webhook endpoint for QR/manual check-ins
- Member validation and debt status checking
- Automatic WhatsApp confirmation
- Contextual collection flagging for debtors
- 90-minute delayed feedback survey scheduling

**Daily Collection Flow** (`collection-flow.json`):
- Cron trigger at 9:00 AM daily
- Groups overdue payments by days (D0/D3/D7/D14+)
- Sends appropriate WhatsApp template per segment
- D14+ escalates to human with automatic incident ticket creation
- Tracks collection attempts and effectiveness

**Contextual Collection Flow** (`contextual-collection.json`):
- Triggered by check-ins with debt
- 90-minute wait for optimal post-workout timing
- Re-validates debt still exists (in case paid during workout)
- Rate limit checking before sending
- Empathetic messaging for better conversion

## Technical Highlights

### Architecture
- **Clean separation of concerns** with modular design
- **Scalable infrastructure** ready for production growth
- **Queue-based processing** for reliable async operations
- **Comprehensive error handling** throughout all modules

### Security
- Row Level Security (RLS) on all database tables
- WhatsApp webhook signature verification (HMAC SHA256)
- Rate limiting to prevent spam (2 messages/day per user)
- Business hours enforcement (9-21h only)
- Opt-out compliance built-in

### Performance
- 60+ database indexes for fast queries
- Redis-backed message queue with retry logic
- Materialized views for dashboard metrics
- Optimized SQL functions for KPI calculations

### Documentation
- Complete setup guides for n8n configuration
- Database schema documentation with comments
- API endpoint documentation
- Template usage guidelines
- Comprehensive diagnostic report (400+ lines)

## Deliverables

**Files Created**: 28 files, ~8,500 lines of code
- 10 configuration files
- 6 documentation files
- 5 SQL scripts
- 7 JavaScript modules
- 3 n8n workflow JSONs

**Documentation**: 
- `docs/INFORME_DIAGNOSTICO.md` - Complete diagnostic and audit report
- `docs/setup/n8n-configuration.md` - n8n setup guide
- `whatsapp/templates/README.md` - Template documentation
- Database schema comments and README files

## Testing & Validation

All implemented components are:
- ✅ Syntax validated
- ✅ Following best practices and coding standards
- ✅ Properly documented with inline comments
- ✅ Ready for immediate deployment
- ✅ Include sample data for testing

## Next Steps

This PR completes **Phase 1 (27% of total project)**. Remaining work:
- **Phase 2** (Prompts 6-10): Core features - Reservations, Feedback engine, Professor panel, Replacements, Valley promotions
- **Phase 3** (Prompts 11-15): Interfaces - QR landing, Kiosk, Real-time KPIs, Utility scripts, Testing suite, Final documentation

**Estimated time to complete**: 5.5-7.5 additional hours

## How to Use

1. **Install dependencies**: `npm install`
2. **Configure environment**: Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in credentials
3. **Start infrastructure**: `docker-compose up -d`
4. **Run migrations**: Execute SQL scripts in `database/migrations/`
5. **Import n8n workflows**: Import JSON files from `n8n-workflows/`
6. **Start API**: `npm start`

See `docs/setup/n8n-configuration.md` for detailed setup instructions.

body:
This PR fixes two specific UI issues in the Egresados portal:

## Problem 1: Navbar not flush with top edge
The navbar had unwanted green space above it, preventing it from being properly positioned at the very top of the screen. This was caused by `padding: 2rem` on the `#root` element in `App.css`, which pushed the entire application content down despite the navbar having `fixed top-0` positioning.

**Fix**: Removed the padding from `#root` and set proper dimensions for full-screen layout.

## Problem 2: WelcomeEgresado page appearing as centered card
The welcome page was displaying as a white rounded rectangle with shadow, centered on the screen like a floating card, instead of using the full viewport like a normal web page. This was caused by:
- `max-w-4xl` limiting the content width
- `bg-white rounded-3xl shadow-2xl` creating card styling
- `items-center justify-center` centering the content

**Fix**: Replaced the card styling with a full-width layout using `bg-white/90 backdrop-blur-sm` that maintains readability while removing the floating card appearance.

## Changes Made
- **`front/src/App.css`**: Updated `#root` styles to remove padding and enable full-screen layout
- **`front/src/pages/Egresado/WelcomeEgresado.jsx`**: Replaced card-style container with full-width layout

## Screenshots

**Before**: Navbar had green space above it and WelcomeEgresado appeared as a centered card

**After - Home Page**: Navbar now flush with top edge
![Home Page After Fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd4ed718-90eb-46b5-b7ab-7768ae7f89f9)

**After - WelcomeEgresado Page**: Full-screen layout without card effect
![WelcomeEgresado After Fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f30edfeb-fd94-4cf1-ad88-3f791192c945)

The changes are minimal and surgical, maintaining all existing functionality while achieving the desired full-screen appearance with proper navbar positioning.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> New persistence path affects event ordering and restart correctness for strategies; behavior is heavily tested but adds sqlx/SQLite and subtle backfill/live boundary edge cases.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **persistence** pipeline so block-aware collectors can survive restarts without re-syncing from genesis. Call **`.with_persistence(store)`** on collectors that implement **`PersistableCollector`** (notably **`EventCollector`**, which now exposes indexed live streams, **`query_range`**, and **`tip`**).
> 
> On **`subscribe`**, **`Persisted`** chains **replay** (SQLite archive, first subscribe only) → **RPC backfill** to the reported tip → **live** tail, while writing completed blocks transactionally via a pluggable **`Store`** (**`SqliteStore`** + **`sqlx`**). Schemas are derived from Solidity event names and serde fields, with optional overrides and a lossless **`_payload`** column for replay.
> 
> Also documents the feature in **README**, adds **`persistence_example`**, extensive **`tests/persistence`**, and pins Foundry to **`v1.7.1`** in CI to avoid GitHub rate-limit failures.

author: lifefloating
body:
## TLDR

Implemented automatic truncation of oversized log entries before sending to Google Cloud Logging to prevent failures from exceeding the 256KB hard limit. Large fields are intelligently truncated while preserving critical diagnostic metadata, with full telemetry tracking for observability.

## Dive Deeper

### Problem

Google Cloud Logging has a hard 256KB (262,144 bytes) limit per log entry. When telemetry logs contain large payloads (e.g., long API responses, large function arguments), they can exceed this limit and cause logging failures, resulting in lost telemetry data.

### Solution

**Core Implementation (`gcp-exporters.ts` - 173 new lines):**

1. **Size calculation and threshold management:**
   - Calculates log entry size using `TextEncoder` to get accurate byte counts
   - Uses 200KB threshold (leaving 56KB buffer for metadata overhead)
   - Hard limit awareness: 256KB (262,144 bytes)

2. **Smart truncation algorithm (`truncateLargeAttributes`):**
   - **Phase 1:** Truncates known large fields first:
     - `response_text`, `function_args`, `prompt`, `request_text`, `message`
     - Strings > 1000 chars → truncated to 500 chars + marker
     - Objects > 1000 chars (JSON) → truncated to 500 chars + marker
   - **Phase 2:** If still over limit, removes all non-critical fields
   - **Always preserved:** Critical diagnostic fields:
     - `session.id`, `user.email`, `event.name`, `event.timestamp`
     - `model`, `error.message`, `error.type`, `prompt_id`
     - `function_name`, `tool_name`, `status_code`, `duration_ms`

3. **Metadata tracking:**
   - Adds `_log_entry_truncated: true` flag
   - Records `_original_size_bytes` and `_truncated_size_bytes`
   - Lists `_truncated_fields` (comma-separated)
   - Logs warning in DEBUG_MODE

4. **Error handling:**
   - Gracefully handles JSON.stringify failures (circular references)
   - Returns max limit on calculation errors to trigger truncation

**Telemetry Event Tracking (`LogEntryTruncatedEvent`):**

Added comprehensive telemetry to track when and how truncation occurs:
- `original_size_bytes`: Size before truncation
- `truncated_size_bytes`: Size after truncation
- `truncated_fields`: List of fields that were truncated
- `event_type`: Type of event that was truncated (e.g., 'api_response')

**Clearcut Logger Integration:**
- Added `LOG_ENTRY_TRUNCATED` event type
- 4 new event metadata keys (109-112) for tracking truncation details
- `logLogEntryTruncatedEvent()` method to record truncation events


## Reviewer Test Plan

1. **Run unit tests:**
   ```bash
   cd packages/core
   npm test -- gcp-exporters.test.ts
   ```
   All 26 tests should pass (18 existing + 8 new).

2. **Test with large payloads:**
   - Create a scenario that generates a large API response (> 200KB)
   - Verify logs are successfully sent to GCP Cloud Logging
   - Check for `_log_entry_truncated` metadata in logs
   - Confirm critical fields (`session.id`, `event.name`) are preserved

3. **Debug mode verification:**
   ```bash
   DEBUG_MODE=true npm run start
   ```
   - Generate large telemetry events
   - Look for console warnings about truncation

## ✅ 작업 개요 - 개인 보따리 로직 개선 (데이터, 도메인 레이어)
## 🎯 관련 이슈 - Closed #556
## 🔍 상세 내용 - 도메인 레이어에서 처리하던 데이터 관련 로직(예: 템플릿 생성 실패 시 보따리 삭제)을 데이터 레이어로 위임 - `@Transaction`, `@Relation` 등을 이용한 로직 구현
## 💬 기타 참고사항 - 테스트 필요
## Summary by CodeRabbit - 신기능 - 템플릿에서 제목과 아이템 이름만으로 보따리와 아이템을 한 번에 생성/저장 가능. - 개선 - 보따리 목록·상세에서 아이템과 알람 정보를 함께 확인 가능. - 생성·저장 작업이 트랜잭션으로 처리되어 데이터 일관성 향상. - 템플릿 생성 화면에서 아이템이 없는 보따리는 목록에서 제외되어 선택이 명확해짐. - 보따리 조회 흐름 단순화로 로딩 동작 개선. - UI 변경 - 개인 아이템 편집 화면의 확인(저장) 버튼 및 일부 확인 다이얼로그 제거; 항목 저장 흐름이 즉시 처리되도록 변경.

author: kjappelbaum
body:
## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce a comprehensive reaction kinetics environment for fitting and analyzing experimental oxygen evolution data. Define a Reaction class and ODE system builder, implement parameter fitting via differential evolution, and provide KineticTools utilities for describing data, performing fits, evaluating trends, modifying networks, and visualizing results. Add a KineticFittingEnv to load and standardize HDF5 experimental datasets, initialize a default reaction network, and track fit history. Include unit tests for data loading, environment setup, reaction network validation, and environment state management.

New Features:
- Implement Reaction dataclass and create_ode_system to model light- and dark-driven reaction networks
- Add fit_reaction_network function using differential evolution and ODE integration for parameter estimation
- Provide KineticTools with methods for experimental data description, single/all experiment fitting, trend evaluation, network modification, and fit visualization
- Introduce KineticFittingEnv to load HDF5 experimental data, standardize metadata, initialize default reaction network, and manage fit history
- Initialize a default reaction network based on Akhtar 2016 scheme
- Standardize metadata fields including Ru, S2O8 concentrations and irradiance
- Add unit tests for HDF5 data loading, environment loading, reaction network structure, and environment state methods

Tests:
- Add tests for HDF5 file structure and data value validation
- Add tests for KineticFittingEnv initialization, data shapes, metadata mapping, and state/reset behavior
- Add tests to validate initial reaction network fields and ranges

author: pebcac
body:
Fixes #191 

## Issue
The copy button was appearing above captioned code blocks instead of being positioned within the code block itself.

When Org mode exports code blocks with captions, the HTML structure includes a `<label class="org-src-name">` element before the `<pre>` element. The previous implementation used `prepend()` on `.org-src-container`, which inserted the copy button before the label, causing it to appear above the caption rather than within the code block area.

## Solution
This PR implements three key changes:

1. **Changed button insertion method**: Modified from `prepend()` on the container to `append()` on the `pre.src` element. This ensures the button is always placed inside the code block, regardless of whether a caption is present.

2. **Added relative positioning to pre.src**: Added CSS rule to position `pre.src` relatively, ensuring the absolutely positioned button is placed correctly relative to the code block itself.

3. **Improved copy handler**: Updated the click handler to:
   - Use `closest()` instead of `parent().parent()` for more reliable DOM traversal
   - Clone the `pre` element before extracting text to exclude the copy button text from the copied content

## Result
The copy button now appears consistently in the top-right corner of all code blocks, with or without captions.

## Testing
Tested with:
- Code blocks with captions
- Code blocks without captions
- Long captions that wrap to multiple lines

body:
# Bounty #361 – OM1 × Three.js Mini Simulator

Adds a minimal Three.js simulator + Node/WS bridge compatible with an OM1-style loop.

## What's included

### Bridge (Express + WS):
- **POST /action** `{ v, w }` → returns `{ reward, done, info:{ steps, collisions, minDist }}`
- **POST /reset**
- **WS /ws** broadcasts state →50ms: pose, sensors (beams), reward, done

### Client (React + Three.js):
- Renders bot + obstacles, visualizes beams, HUD (minDist, reward), WASD controls

## Demo
**Video**: https://youtu.be/TQtGVfoVooE

Watch the full walkthrough showing:
- Bridge and client setup
- Keyboard control (W/A/S/D)
- Sensor visualization
- Collision detection
- Real-time HUD updates

## How to run

### Bridge:
```bash
cd tools/threejs-sim/bridge
npm install
npm start  # Runs on port 8081
```

### Client:
```bash
cd tools/threejs-sim/client
npm install
npm run dev  # Runs on http://localhost:5173
```

Open browser at http://localhost:5173 and use W/A/S/D keys to control the robot.

### API Example:
```bash
# Move forward
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/action \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"v": 0.05, "w": 0.0}'

# Reset environment
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/reset
```

## Testing with Python
```bash
cd tools/threejs-sim
python3 example_agent.py
```

## Hygiene
- Removed `.vite/` and all lockfiles from tracking
- Tightened `.gitignore`
- README cleaned (no conflict markers)

## Documentation
- `docs/bounty-361/README.md` - Complete documentation with API reference
- `docs/bounty-361/QUICKSTART.md` - 5-minute setup guide
- `tools/threejs-sim/README.md` - Project overview
- `tools/threejs-sim/example_agent.py` - Python control example

## Notes
Supersedes #410 (closed).

Closes #361.

author: eurolew
body:
## Description

Fix an OOM crash loop that occurs due to too big variable sizes

before: 
- submitted even 20 PIs with variables of size 1MB would crash loop and block the system

after:
- it takes around 300-400 PIs of variable size 1MB before crashing the system (this are all submitted within 10s), this sort of OOM is expected as the load as extremely high for a pod with only 1GB of memory.
- Even after the crash it does NOT crash loop, as the batch request is now bounded by a rough memory estimate when the pod restarts the batch request doesn't immediately fill up and crash again as now there is a low threshold to flush. (only a dozen big variables is sufficient to trigger a flush).

Is it correct to backport to stable/8.8 and not the release branch?

## Related issues

closes #37845

- Copied [from discord](https://discord.com/channels/945714351841607690/1421091583704432660/1422526348689281135): Investigated the issue if I can use target_os, target_arch to distinguish brevis pico from other zkvms. I believe the ans is not. 
  Because pico themselves use [**riscv32im-risc0-zkvm-elf** as the target string](https://github.com/brevis-network/pico/blob/main/sdk/cli/src/build/build.rs#L82).
As a result, `target_arch == riscv32`, `target_vendor == risc0`, `target_os == zkvm`, same as risc0 vm 😓. Here is an example of their check in [pico sha256 lib](https://github.com/brevis-network/hashes/blob/pico-patch-v1.0.1-sha2-v0.10.8/sha2/src/sha256.rs#L4-L6).
  I raised this issue to them this morning, but there will be a lot of changes, across multiple repos, if they decide to address this issue. So I am not hopeful they will address this anytime soon and we probably have to resolve to add our own (feature) flag.

author: neulus
body:
in line 831 of `emulator.cpp`, `sltu` instruction is defined as:

```cpp
case SLTU: rf[i.a1.reg] = rf[i.a2.reg] + rf[i.a3.reg]; break;
```

which is same as `add` instruction.

however, according to the [reference card](https://www.cs.sfu.ca/~ashriram/Courses/CS295/assets/notebooks/RISCV/RISCV_CARD.pdf) of risc-v, `sltu` is defined as `rd = (rs1 < rs2) ? 1 : 0` which makes current implementation incorrect.

i changed it to handle the instruction correctly.

```cpp
case SLTU: rf[i.a1.reg] = rf[i.a2.reg] < rf[i.a3.reg] ? 1 : 0; break;
```

---

we can demonstrate the issue and the fix by using the simple assembly:

```s
.text
start:
    li t0 1
    li t1 2
    sltu t2 t0 t1
    hcf
```

### before the fix

```bash
Next: sltu t2, t0, t1
[inst:      5 pc:     16, src line    5]
>>
>> rf[x07] 0 -> 3
```

here we can see the `t2` register is incorrectly set to `3`.

### after the fix

```bash
Next: sltu t2, t0, t1
[inst:      5 pc:     16, src line    5]
>>
>> rf[x07] 0 -> 1
```

in this case, the `t2` register is set to `1` correctly.

author: bluepal-ashok-patcha
body:
This commit refactors the security architecture to implement JWT validation within each individual microservice, as requested. It also addresses the CSRF issue and updates the customer registration flow.

Key changes:
- **Per-Service JWT Validation:** Each resource service (`user-service`, `restaurant-service`, `order-service`, `delivery-service`) now has its own `JwtUtil`, `JwtAuthenticationFilter`, and `SecurityConfig` to validate tokens independently.
- **Secure Identity Handling:** All controllers have been updated to extract the authenticated user's ID from the `SecurityContextHolder` principal, removing the need for insecure request headers or path variables.
- **CSRF Disabled:** Added a security configuration to the API Gateway to explicitly disable CSRF, resolving the "An expected CSRF token cannot be found" error.
- **Customer Registration Update:** The `POST /auth/register` endpoint no longer accepts a `role` and now defaults to creating users with the `CUSTOMER` role.
- **Updated Dependencies:** Added `spring-boot-starter-security` and `jjwt` dependencies to all resource services.
- **Updated Postman Guide:** The guide has been updated to reflect the new API structure.

author: haplee
body:
The application was failing on Vercel with a `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'pybabel'` because the `vercel.py` entry point was attempting to compile translation files (`.po` to `.mo`) at runtime. The `pybabel` command is not available in the Vercel serverless environment's PATH.

This commit resolves the issue by shifting to a pre-compilation strategy:
1.  The `.mo` translation files have been compiled locally and are now included in the repository.
2.  The runtime compilation logic, which executed `subprocess.run(['pybabel', ...])`, has been completely removed from `vercel.py`.

This ensures that the application has access to the necessary translation files without needing to perform compilation during startup, fixing the deployment error and making the startup process more efficient.
